detailed_rationale:
KNR Constructions is a Hyderabad-based EPC contractor building highways, flyovers, bridges, and irrigation/urban-water infrastructure via EPC, BOT and Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) structures. Unlike Ashoka Buildcon in this batch, KNRCON's very low PE (8.1x) is not primarily a one-off-driven optical illusion - it reflects a genuine, severe order-execution slowdown: FY26 revenue of Rs.2,698cr against Rs.4,753cr in FY25 is a real 43% decline, matching the quant model's -43.2% one-year revenue growth figure, and ROCE has fallen from 26% (Mar 2024) to just 10.4% recently - a dramatic, real deterioration in capital efficiency, not an accounting artifact.

The company recently sold its 99.9% stake in subsidiary KRIPL to Indus Infra Trust for Rs.227cr (June 2026), a standard HAM-developer practice of monetizing completed road assets into an InvIT to recycle capital, but this also means future annuity income from that asset is gone. One quarter (Mar 2025) showed profit collapsing to just Rs.8cr alongside an anomalous 87% effective tax rate - a genuine one-off worth flagging, though it does not change the broader picture. Working capital has deteriorated severely (working-capital days 192 to 345, debtor days 78.5 to 109), and debt has nearly doubled (Rs.1,262cr to Rs.2,444cr) over two years even as revenue has been shrinking - a genuinely worrying combination, since rising debt alongside falling revenue and stretched receivables is a classic pattern preceding further stress rather than a temporary dip.

Reverse-DCF: an 8x multiple would ordinarily scream cheap for a business with a 19-26% historical ROE track record, but the current trajectory - order book clearly not being replenished as fast as legacy projects complete, working capital deteriorating, leverage rising - suggests the low multiple is the market correctly pricing a real slowdown, not a mispriced quality business. We would want to see order-book replenishment and working-capital stabilization before treating this cheapness as a genuine opportunity.
recommendation_rationale: The quant model scores this Sell on both the 3-year (37.8) and 1-year (34.6) composites, driven by the near-bottom-percentile growth scores that reflect the real 43% revenue decline. Our research corroborates that this is a genuine operating slowdown rather than a value trap illusion or one-off distortion, and the concurrent rise in debt and working-capital stress argues against treating the low PE as a margin of safety. We confirm Sell.
summary: KNR Constructions is going through a genuine, severe order-execution slowdown - revenue fell about 43% in the latest year and returns on capital have dropped from the mid-20s to about 10% - while debt has nearly doubled and working capital has deteriorated sharply. The statistically low 8x P/E does not look like a bargain here; it looks like the market correctly pricing a real slowdown in a business whose new order intake has not kept pace with completing projects. We recommend keeping this a Sell.
positive_para: KNR Constructions has a long track record of strong historical returns (19-26% ROE/ROCE in recent years) and continues to actively recycle capital through asset monetization (the KRIPL stake sale to an InvIT), which can strengthen the balance sheet if proceeds are used to pay down the recently-added debt. Rising retail (public) shareholding suggests some investor appetite for the story at current depressed levels.
negative_para: Revenue fell approximately 43% year-on-year, a severe decline consistent with new order intake lagging well behind project completions, and ROCE has fallen from 26% to roughly 10% in just two years. Debt has nearly doubled over the same period even as the topline shrank, and working-capital days have deteriorated sharply (192 to 345) alongside rising debtor days - a combination of falling revenue, rising leverage, and weakening collections that typically precedes further stress rather than resolving quickly.
reverse_dcf_judgment: An 8x multiple would normally look cheap against a historical 19-26% ROE, but ROCE has already fallen to about 10% and is still trending down, while debt is rising against a shrinking revenue base. We read this as the market correctly discounting a genuine slowdown rather than an opportunity to buy quality at a depressed price.
